title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: STNFS discrete log in GT

claims.statement: For each production instance with nonidentity P in G1 and z in GT (including z=1), compute g=e(P,Q0)=pairing(Q0,P,final_exponentiate=True), solve a=log_g z with the published Special-Tower Number Field Sieve in F_{p^12} using the Guillevic-Singh BLS12-381 polynomial and Table 10 parameters, return Q=[a]Q0, and verify e(P,Q)=z. STNFS relation collection, linear algebra and descent are Las Vegas and retried inside the charged expectation, so success probability is 1. The published GS21 total 2^126 (recomputed 2^126.146602479037 from the published parameters) is converted conservatively to scalar instructions by 8 instructions/cycle (the widest current AArch64 retirement width) times 16, where 16 covers the worst measured sieving constant (GGMT17: about 7.08 cycles per GS21 model operation) plus a 1.25x allowance for descent, ECM, failures, filtering, verification and output, giving R <= 2^133.146602 instruction equivalents. With H=0 for the dominant work (the final verification pairings use fewer than 2^16 reference operations and are covered by the conversion margin) and C=20,000 instructions per target operation, the total is 2^118.858891 target-group-operation equivalents. Peak memory is at most 2^72.389801 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^118.858891 target-operation equivalents (the field-only computation dominates, charged in full with no reuse credit); nonuniform advice is 0. No auxiliary powers are used. The score is log2(W)=118.858891. This is an analytic reproduction of a published cost model, not a production-size execution.

experiments.purpose: Recompute the GS21 BLS-381 STNFS relation-collection, linear-algebra and total cost from the published Table 10 parameters, then recompute the instruction-equivalent conversion (8 instructions/cycle times 16 for the worst measured sieving calibration plus the omitted-phase allowance) and normalized score in this submission's ledger. The script asserts that the recomputed sieving space matches the published 2^124.08, that the total is within 0.25 bits of the published 2^126, and that the normalized score matches the claim to 1e-6. It is arithmetic evidence for the cost claim, not an attack run.
